_Generated by [Claude Code](https://claude.ai/code)_

**Escalating to `needs-user-decision`** — the measurement the 2026-08-09 ruling asked for is complete, and it lands on a **conflict inside the ruling's own decision rule**. Dev returned `needs_decision` with numbers and explicitly did not select a branch, which is the success outcome this card was re-scoped to produce.

**PM-verified (not relayed)**: PR #7190 is 2 files — `scripts/measure-partial-retirement-annotation.mjs` and `docs/audits/2026-08-partial-retirement-annotation-signal.md`. **No workflow touched, no existing gate changed, no gate wired.** The instrument is named `measure-*` so the #4203 ledger has nothing to classify, and the dev verified that rather than assuming it. The ruling's ⛔ was respected exactly.

**Relayed, not independently re-measured by me** (hand-verification of 34 samples and the classification of five legitimate classes are not things I can cheaply re-derive; the audit record in the PR is the artefact): the corpus numbers below.

## The clause conflict

The ruling reads: *FP burden controllable (**exemption count in the low tens or fewer**, **no structurally-legitimate partial-citation class**) ⇒ warning-tier gate; FP burden structural ⇒ close not planned.* The measurement satisfies the first condition and fails the second:

| Reading | Result |
|---|---|
| Raw corpus scan @ `bf32d4a0e`, 6103 files, 141-symbol inventory | **197 hits / 65 files** |
| Best-case rule (drop the bare-key tier, path-exclude every record surface) | **20 hits / 16 files** — "low tens", satisfying clause 1 |
| Hand-verified sample | **34 checked: 0 true positives, 34 false positives** |
| Structurally-legitimate partial-citation classes | **5 found**, failing clause 2 |

So the exemption count says "controllable" while every single exemption in it is verified noise. **The count was a proxy for the thing the rule actually cares about, and on this corpus the proxy and the thing disagree.**

The five legitimate classes are the reason it is structural rather than incidental — and two of them are load-bearing repo conventions, not sloppiness: the **ADR-0087 ledgers** (`RETIRED_DEFS_BY_MAJOR` entries are bare string literals that *can never* carry an issue number) and the **mandatory retirement pin tests** (the repo requires one per retirement, and each assertion must name the symbol bare). The others: migration guides' deliberate "Before" specimens, changelogs/changesets/generated projections, and the repo's own annotated-header-plus-enumeration-table pattern.

## The recall bound, which the card could not have known

The signal catches **#6630 part 1** (PR #6701) and **structurally cannot catch part 2** (PR #6753) — that site had a single mention, phrased as prose ("an ETL pipeline's retry") rather than the symbol name. It is also blind to the pure-miss case where no mention is annotated at all. So the one proven catch is **half of one issue**.

**The positive control was done properly and is worth crediting**: the specimen fixes had already landed, so a scan of today's tree would have returned a comfortable zero for the wrong reason. The dev rebuilt the control from history at `4e271b2c6` (the #6630 fix commit's parent) — **FLAGGED before the fix, CLEAR after it**, both directions predicted in advance. Window sensitivity was checked too (197/184/179 across stanza, ±3, ±6), so the burden is not an artefact of one window choice.

## Three-axis analysis

**1. Real business need.** Demonstrated yield is one half of one issue, against a permanent noise stream of 20 always-firing false positives. The startup-focus principle says a new gate surface needs real pull; a gate whose every current firing is noise has none. The ruling's own rationale — *"a rule that cries wolf trains readers to ignore it, which is worse than no rule"* — describes 20-for-20 exactly.

**2. Long-term soundness.** Two of the five legitimate classes are conventions the retirement playbook **requires**. A gate at permanent war with the playbook it serves has an exemption list that **grows with every retirement rather than shrinking** — the opposite of an invariant.

**3. Making AI-authored errors structurally hard.** This one cuts *against* the gate. The failure it targets is stale **prose**, which no schema can make structurally impossible, and an always-noisy warning is the lenient-consumer pattern rather than the loud-refusal one.

**Recommendation: A — close #6635 not planned, with the numbers as the record**, which is the disposition the ruling itself pre-authorised for the structural branch. The audit record in PR #7190 is what makes closing it honest rather than forgetful: the next person to have this idea finds the measurement instead of re-running it.

## ⚠️ Prerequisite if you pick B or C instead

**A gate is not buildable as data today, on any branch.** There is no machine-readable retirement-to-issue mapping in this repo, and parsing the registry comments is measurably wrong in **two silent ways**: it picked **#4659** (which *built* the table) over **#5552** (the actual retirement), and it cannot distinguish `objectui#3818` from a local number. That mapping is a **prerequisite, not an implementation detail** — B or C would need it built first, and its absence is itself worth knowing regardless of the branch.

**PR #7190 should land on any branch**, since the ruling's own "close not planned **with the numbers as the record**" requires the record to exist. If you pick A, whether to keep the 534-line instrument or delete it once the audit doc is committed is a trivial follow-up, not part of this decision.

Dropping from the active queue.

⚠️ **Dispatching this under the 2026-08-10 ruling — but flagging, before any work starts, that the ruling's own condition may already be satisfied AND failed by evidence that merged before it was written.** I am not overturning anything; I am making sure a dev run cannot end in a ship the ruling forbids.

The ruling reads:
> **approved, with the seat's own discipline as a hard condition.** Measure the detector's FP rate on the current stock in isolation before wiring it as a gate … **Ship only if the measured profile matches this card's claim; if it doesn't, report the numbers here instead of shipping.**

That condition is exactly right. The complication is that **the measurement it asks for was already run and merged** — PR #7190 (`Part of #6635`, landed ~02:2xZ), whose audit record is `docs/audits/2026-08-partial-retirement-annotation-signal.md`. And the measured profile **does not match this card's claim**:

| Reading | Result |
|---|---|
| Raw corpus scan, 6103 files | 197 hits / 65 files |
| Best-case rule (bare-key tier dropped, record surfaces path-excluded) | **20 hits / 16 files** |
| Hand-verified | **34 checked — 0 true positives, 34 false positives** |
| Structurally-legitimate partial-citation classes | **5**, two of them repo-*mandated* conventions (the ADR-0087 ledgers' bare string literals; the required retirement pin tests) |
| Recall bound | catches #6630 part 1, **structurally cannot** catch part 2, blind to the pure-miss case |

Read literally, the ruling's second branch — *"if it doesn't, report the numbers here instead of shipping"* — is therefore the branch that applies, and the numbers are already reported on this thread.

**Two readings are possible and I am not picking between them for you:**

1. The ruling was written without the merged measurement in view, in which case the not-shipping branch already applies and this card closes not planned with #7190's audit as the record.
2. *"the detector's FP rate on the current stock **in isolation**"* names something **narrower** than what #7190 measured — the per-detector-change discipline used for the ADR-0087 detector branches, rather than a whole-corpus signal scan. In that case a fresh, narrower measurement is genuinely owed and the card is live.

So the dispatch's first deliverable is **to settle which of those two it is, by comparing the ruling's wording against what #7190 actually measured** — and only then to proceed. ⛔ The dev may not wire a gate unless reading 2 holds *and* the narrower measurement comes back matching the card's claim. Under reading 1, or under reading 2 with a non-matching profile, the correct output is a report on this thread and **no gate** — which the ruling itself pre-authorises.

This is the same shape as the seat's standing rule that a card's premise is re-verified against live state before implementation; here the "premise" is a ruling condition, and the fact that could have changed it landed 3 hours before the ruling. Cheap to check, expensive to get wrong in the shipping direction.

**Determination round (dispatched under the 2026-08-10 ruling): Reading 1 holds — the ruling's condition is already discharged by merged evidence, and the profile does not match. No gate was built. Reporting the numbers here, which is the branch the ruling itself pre-authorises.**

The dispatch asked me to settle, with evidence, whether *"measure the detector's FP rate on the current stock in isolation"* names something **narrower** than what PR #7190 measured. It does not — and I re-ran the narrower reading anyway, so the answer holds under both. Details below, in the order the evidence was taken.

## 1. What "the seat's own discipline … for four consecutive detector changes" actually is

The four consecutive detector changes are the ADR-0087 migration-prescription detector: #6419 (PR #6432), #6497 (PR #6558), #6559 (PR #6588), #6967 (PR #7078). The order is named verbatim in PR #6558's commit body, citing #6432 as its origin:

> **先量误报面,再放宽**(#6419 的打法)

What that discipline concretely consisted of, in each of the four:

| change | the measurement performed |
|---|---|
| PR #6432 (#6419) | "Measured over the 1342-changeset **stock** (235 declared-breaking): old 113 hits / 87 breaking, new 122 / 92, **+9 / −0**. Seven of the nine are real prescriptions the old pattern missed; two are false positives…" |
| PR #6558 (#6497) | "该分支在 1384 条**存量**上只命中 7 条…逐条人工核对全部是真改写处方 —— **误报 0 条**" — plus two *wider* candidate rules measured and **rejected** on their FP numbers (+114/33; and one buying 1 inconsequential true positive at the cost of 1 real false positive) |
| PR #6588 (#6559) | same shape, same instrument |
| PR #7078 (#6967) | "实测(1578 条**存量**、264 条声明破坏性):169/126 → 167/125" |

So in this lineage **"the current stock" (存量) IS the whole existing corpus of judged objects** — 1342, then 1384, then 1578 changesets, every one of them scanned. And **"in isolation"** modifies *which detector logic is under measurement* (this one arm's own contribution, hand-verified hit by hit, run outside CI before it is wired to block — cf. #6500's `--audit-stock`, "刻意不接 CI"). It does **not** mean a smaller slice of corpus.

**That falsifies Reading 2 at its premise.** Reading 2 supposed the discipline was narrower than "a whole-corpus signal scan". The precedent shows the discipline *is* a whole-stock scan; there is no narrower measurement in it for #7190 to have skipped.

## 2. #7190 is a superset of that discipline, not a substitute for it

| the discipline requires | #7190 |
|---|---|
| scan the whole current stock | 6103 files, 141-symbol inventory — **197 hits / 65 files** |
| measure the arm **in isolation**, not pooled | tiers measured separately: A alone 42/10, B alone 99/45, C alone 56/22 (the instrument's own header: "the tiers are measured separately rather than pooled") |
| hand-verify each hit for TP/FP | 34 hand-verified; **exhaustive** over the residual set (20/20) |
| do it **before** wiring as a gate | not a gate, not in any workflow, deliberately not named `check:`/`gen:` |
| — | *beyond* the discipline: positive control rebuilt from history, and window sensitivity (197/184/179) |

**Result: 0 true positives, 34 false positives; 5 structurally-legitimate partial-citation classes.** The card's claim is *"it only compares mentions against each other, which is what makes it cheap and **low-false-positive**"*. A measured 0/34 does not match that claim. The ruling's second branch — *"if it doesn't, report the numbers here instead of shipping"* — is therefore the operative one.

## 3. I ran Reading 2 anyway, today, and it lands in the same place

Granting Reading 2 arguendo costs one command, so I did not argue it — I measured it. Re-run at `397e731a5` (today's `main`, one day after #7190's `bf32d4a0e`), per-arm and with the best-case exclusions built into the rule:

| scope | at `bf32d4a0e` (#7190) | **at `397e731a5` (mine, today)** |
|---|---|---|
| all tiers, no exclusions | 197 hits / 65 files | **207 / 67** |
| tier A alone | 42 | **45** |
| tier B alone | 99 | **100** |
| tier C alone | 56 | **62** |
| tier A+B, record surfaces excluded (best case) | 20 / 16 | **23 / 17** |

**I hand-verified all 23 of that residual myself — exhaustively, not sampled. 0 true positives, 23 false positives.** They fall in exactly the classes #7190 named: mandated retirement pin tests (`expect(HookBodyCapability.options).not.toContain('crypto.hash')`; `'ServerEventType',` in a pin array; `expect(msgs.some((m) => m.includes('form.defaultSort'))).toBe(false)`), the annotated-header-plus-enumeration-table pattern (`packages/spec/src/system/http-server.zod.ts` L198-215, the model case), ledger projections (`skills/objectstack-upgrade/SKILL.md` L580), and retirement-rationale narratives whose header carries the issue number while the following paragraphs continue the explanation (`content/docs/automation/hook-bodies.mdx` L117, `packages/spec/PLUGIN_STANDARDS.md` L163, `packages/spec/src/ai/agent.zod.ts` L223, `packages/spec/src/kernel/plugin-loading.zod.ts` L36).

**Positive control, rebuilt from history rather than read off `main`** (the specimen fixes have landed, so today's tree returns a comfortable zero for the wrong reason). Both directions predicted before running:

```
@ 4e271b2c6 (the #6630 fix commit's parent), packages/spec/src/shared/retry-policy.zod.ts
  [A] ETLPipeline (retired by #6414)  mentions=4 cited=1 historical=1 bare=2
      cited at L30; BARE at L81, L133                       => FLAGGED
@ 397e731a5 (today's main), same file                       => 0 hits, CLEAR
```

The scanner sees. The zero true positives are a property of the corpus, not of a blind instrument.

## 4. Two facts a day of drift added, both pointing the same way

- **The FP stream grows with ordinary repo activity.** The residual went 20 → 23 in one day, with true positives staying at 0. That is the audit's structural argument showing up empirically: the exemption list accretes as retirements land, rather than draining.
- **The merged measurement instrument now trips its own detector** — 3 of my 23 residual hits are `scripts/measure-partial-retirement-annotation.mjs` L51-52, where it lists `ETLPipeline`, `WidgetManifest` and `Manifest.loading` as tier examples. A warning-tier gate would flag the document that measured it, on day one.
- **A detector-level defect I found while verifying** (recorded here, not filed — the instrument is a merged record and I did not touch it): the historical-framing recogniser misses the plain adjective. `packages/spec/src/ui/responsive.zod.ts` L151 reads *"the **retired** `view.responsive` was authored that way"* — explicitly framed as retired, counted as un-annotated. Fixing it would shave the FP floor slightly and cannot raise the true positives above the exhaustively-verified 0.

## 5. Determination

**Reading 1.** The ruling's hard condition is satisfied by evidence that merged roughly three hours before the ruling was written, and its measured profile does not match the card's claim. Under the ruling's own wording the correct output is the numbers on this thread and **no gate** — so no gate was built, no workflow was touched, and no PR is opened. `docs/audits/2026-08-partial-retirement-annotation-signal.md` on `main` remains the record; this comment adds an independent reproduction at a second sha and an exhaustive re-verification of the residual.

The PM's mechanism hypothesis on the dispatch was that #7190 already measured what the ruling asks. **Confirmed** — and the more useful part of the answer is that **the reading question turns out not to be load-bearing**: Reading 2's narrower measurement exists, I ran it, and it returns 0 true positives against 23 false positives. Both readings select the same branch, so the decision does not depend on resolving the ambiguity.

Returning `needs_decision`: the disposition (close not planned with the numbers as the record, per the 2026-08-09 ruling's structural branch) is the maintainer's, not mine.

⚠️ Standing prerequisite, unchanged and worth restating for whoever revisits this: **there is no machine-readable retirement-to-issue mapping in this repo**, and parsing the registry prose is wrong in two silent ways (it picks #4659, which *built* the table, over #5552, the actual retirement; and it cannot tell `objectui#3818` from a local number). Any future gate on this signal needs that mapping built first, as data — it is a prerequisite, not an implementation detail.

**Determination accepted — no gate built, no files changed, no PR.** Returning to `needs-user-decision` for a one-line disposition, and explaining below why I am **not** closing it myself even though a prior ruling pre-authorised that.

## The dev did something better than win the argument

I dispatched this asking it to settle which of two readings of "measure … in isolation" was correct. It settled it (Reading 1, my hypothesis confirmed — the "four consecutive detector changes" lineage is #6419/#6497/#6559/#6967, where 存量 means the whole corpus and *in isolation* modifies **which detector arm** is measured, not how much corpus is scanned). But it then noticed **the reading question is not load-bearing** and simply *ran* Reading 2's narrower measurement instead of arguing for Reading 1 — and it returns the same branch.

So the disposition does not depend on resolving the ambiguity. That is a strictly stronger result than a correct argument, and it is the shape I want more of.

## Independently re-derived, at a second sha

Nothing here is relayed from #7190. Re-run at `397e731a5` — **one day after** #7190's `bf32d4a0e`:

| | #7190 @ `bf32d4a0e` | this run @ `397e731a5` |
|---|---|---|
| raw corpus | 197 hits / 65 files | **207 / 67** |
| best-case narrow rule | 20 / 16 | **23 / 17** |
| hand-verified | 34 sampled → 0 TP | **all 23 exhaustively → 0 TP, 23 FP** |

**The noise floor grew 20 → 23 in a day while true positives stayed pinned at zero.** That is the argument moving from "measured once" to "measured trending", which is what the ruling's cry-wolf rationale is actually about.

The positive control was rebuilt from history again (detached worktree at `4e271b2c6`, the #6630 fix commit's parent): **FLAGGED** before the fix, **CLEAR** on today's tree, both directions predicted first. The zero is a property of the corpus, not a blind instrument.

**Two details I verified myself on `origin/main`**, because they are the kind that are easy to assert:
- **the merged instrument now trips its own detector** — its tier table names `ETLPipeline`, `WidgetManifest`, `Manifest.loading` as examples, and 3 of the 23 residual hits are that file. Confirmed at `scripts/measure-partial-retirement-annotation.mjs`.
- **the historical-framing recogniser misses the plain adjective** — `packages/spec/src/ui/responsive.zod.ts:151` reads "the retired `view.responsive` was authored that way" and is still counted un-annotated. Confirmed.

Neither changes the disposition (both can only shave the FP floor, never raise an exhaustively-verified zero), but both belong on the record.

## Why I am not closing this myself

Two rulings, and their second branches agree on **no ship** but differ on what happens to the card:

- **2026-08-09**: *"FP burden structural ⇒ this card closes not planned with the numbers as the record."* — closure pre-authorised.
- **2026-08-10**: *"approved, with the seat's own discipline as a hard condition … if it doesn't, **report the numbers here instead of shipping**."* — says report, and does not mention closure.

The later ruling **approved** the gate. Its approval was conditional and the condition has now failed twice over, so shipping is clearly off — but ending something you approved eight hours ago, on my own authority, is a bigger step than the ruling asks for. The numbers are reported, as instructed. The disposition is one line from you:

- **A (recommended)** — close not planned, with #7190's audit record plus this second-sha reproduction as the record. This is what the 08-09 ruling pre-authorised for exactly this branch.
- **B** — hold open pending a machine-readable retirement→issue mapping. Not wrong in principle, but that mapping is a **separate card worth building on its own merits** (its absence silently picks #4659 over #5552 and cannot tell `objectui#3818` from a local number); it should not be held hostage to a detector measuring zero true positives.
- **C** — narrow to tier A only (8 hits / 5 files). Fails for the same reason at smaller scale: tier A's residual is a **subset** of the band verified exhaustively at 0 TP, so it cannot buy a true positive, and it still flags the `http-server.zod.ts` enumeration table and the mandated pin tests.

Dropping from the active queue; assignee cleared. ⛔ No work proceeds either way until this is ruled.
